values.evidence: delta: 'Recompute after each revealed label'; prediction compares threshold-sensitive ordering with fixed IDs, with no benefit when contributions are invariant/unavailable. probe gives matched copies, unchanged interval certificates, sixteen adjudications, seventy minutes, withheld logging and frozen key comparison. This is useful, bounded and discriminating, but O-52506f6a8d6811274ac6's labeled arrows, removable return edge and equal-demand sham are absent; assessment expressly claims no closing-feedback loop. Archive threshold-priority granularity is unspecified, leaving novelty/family unresolved.

claim challenges 'supported rule decision implies a confusion table was built (B→M)'; delta removes confusion cells in favor of summed paired contributions and uncertainty bounds. prediction expects the same supported decisions while the ledger constructs no table; probe compares carriers using identical selected rows, logs withheld attempts and freezes the key. assessment defeats the opening if ledger/bounds disagree with correct rival results and notes sixteen adjudications/seventy minutes may leave unresolved. Source-supported bookkeeping supplies a genuine necessity counterexample/test, distinct from archive counting, selection and uncertainty questions; no speed advantage is established.

claim says 'Counterexample, not an observation: all flagged rows have matching classifier predictions'; assumptions admit actual agreements and other slice deltas are unspecified. Zero contribution then makes zero-access bounds a useful conditional case, but prediction says both workflows advance without explicitly predicting how many accesses the ordinary bounded rival makes. probe cannot demonstrate the proposed counterexample if influential disputed rows exist; this is its explicit defeat. fit='uncertain' is warranted by that indispensable unknown. This specializes archive unresolved-label bounding to invariant contributions, rather than establishing a new causal operation. Necessity challenge is present, but the common differing-observation requirement is only partial.

claim requires every remaining assignment to pass before advance and joint infeasibility before reject; delta gives zero contributions for matching predictions and [-1,1] otherwise. prediction compares threshold-sensitive with fixed-ID ordering; probe logs every selection/withheld result, forbids repeated withheld requests, freezes reports, and stops at sixteen successful adjudications/seventy minutes. assumptions name withheld influential rows, conservative bounds and bookkeeping cost as defeats. This fits ordinary O-017012b1792011ea58c7 and supports a feasible synthetic comparison; the archive's unspecified threshold-focus ranking prevents resolved novelty/family membership.

delta selects a row whose possible resolutions 'most change certification of an acceptance clause'; prediction compares this frontier with gain-slice-first ordering, expecting supported verdict versus unresolved. probe supplies unchanged lower/upper certificates, matched copies, sixteen/seventy caps, accounting and a frozen key comparison. assumptions explicitly defeat advantage when influential rows are withheld, the rival selects equivalent rows or bounds remain inconclusive. Generic creative contract O-08fa691abb50913ec339 is met without efficacy claims. Archive threshold-priority granularity remains ambiguous, so local newness/family is unresolved.

A delta ranks rows that can cross acceptance boundaries and prioritizes the nearest-failure slice. Archive operation prioritizes disputed labels in the threshold-adjacent slice and resolves those most likely to determine a breach. The archive does not specify whether it recomputes per-row influence, so adaptive frontier versus an ordinary ranking refinement cannot be resolved.

B delta removes the confusion-table carrier; prediction tests same decisions without constructed cells. Archive prioritizes labels near a slice boundary and tests inspection ordering. Holding selected rows identical in B isolates carrier necessity from selection efficiency.

C claim removes any adjudication when all flagged predictions agree; archive instead prioritizes disputed rows in a risky slice. Prediction-agreement invariance versus focused label resolution asks a different dependency question.

D delta selects differing-prediction rows by possible decisions, including the -2 slice; archive resolves labels most likely to determine that slice's breach. Without the archive's ranking granularity, decision-bound selection may be a refined implementation of the same prioritization.

E delta computes acceptance-clause influence per row; archive prioritizes disputed labels most likely to determine a slice breach. The archive's scope of influence calculation is unspecified. A different rival order alone does not resolve whether this is a new causal operation.

A uses unresolved contribution intervals and adaptive threshold selection, testing decision resolution against fixed ordering; archive groups paired prediction/label values into counts to reproduce the provisional gain. Label-sensitive point counting alone does not supply A's selection discriminator.

Archive carrier explicitly includes confusion tables and tests reproducing provisional counts. B removes those cells while holding selected rows fixed and predicts identical supported verdicts; table necessity, rather than count reproduction, is the discriminating question.

C prediction-agreement audit removes label access when paired gains are label-invariant; archive counts predictions against provisional labels. The zero-access dependency test is different from reproducing a provisional count.

D moves point-count decision dependence to unresolved-label bounds and tests threshold-sensitive selection versus fixed IDs; archive counting tests reproduction of provisional gain. Their discriminators differ even though both ultimately sum correctness changes.

E carries per-record intervals and tests frontier selection versus gain-first inspection; archive carries provisional confusion counts. Certifying a verdict under residual uncertainty by selective access differs from reproducing the provisional six-count gain.

Archive bounds possible label assignments to determine definite versus unresolved decisions. A shares this certification component, but its explicit intervention recomputes selection priority and compares resolution against identical bounds with fixed IDs. That ordering-efficiency discriminator is additional; component overlap is not whole-card equivalence.

Archive asks whether remaining uncertainty permits a verdict; B asks whether a confusion table is necessary by comparing carriers on identical adjudications. Bounds are shared infrastructure, while absence/presence of constructed confusion cells is B's distinct observation.

C prediction calls its method 'zero-access bounds'; matching predictions make every disputed contribution exactly zero. Archive possible-label bounding already supports definite verdicts when uncertainty cannot change counts. C is the invariant-contribution limiting case with zero needed adjudications; an ordinary bound-based rival may also use zero.

Both retain unresolved-label bounds and unresolved outcomes. D additionally changes which row is inspected next and compares adjudication use with fixed-ID selection under the same conservative rule. Archive's stated discriminator is definite verdict versus remaining uncertainty, rather than ordering efficiency.

Both provide lower/upper certificates. E's changed action selects maximal acceptance-clause influence and compares gain-first ordering; archive's operation only bounds possible outcomes and distinguishes definite from residual uncertainty. Shared certificates do not eliminate the added selection test.

Archive tests provisional versus adjudicated gain in the disagreement-heavy slice. A acknowledges that slice may lose certainty but tests threshold selection versus fixed order across acceptance clauses. Disagreement inspection is an overlap, not its causal discriminator.

B compares table and ledger carriers on identical selected rows; archive inspects disagreements to test whether apparent gains depend on labels. Carrier necessity and disputed-gain dependence predict different observations.

Archive adjudicates annotator disagreements to test gain dependence; C audits classifier prediction agreement to avoid access when all contributions are invariant. Annotator disagreement does not imply classifier disagreement, so the mechanisms are distinct.

D may inspect gain-slice disagreements, but selects by acceptance influence and compares with fixed ordering. Archive compares provisional and adjudicated gains in that slice. The selection-efficiency test remains distinct from measuring label-dependent gain.

E makes gain-first inspection its rival and predicts more certifiable decisions through acceptance-clause influence. Archive merely tests whether that slice's apparent improvement survives adjudication; it supplies no competing selection-efficiency operation.

A changes adjudication ordering and recomputes bounds; B holds selected rows identical while changing confusion-table versus ledger carrier. A predicts ordering advantage, B verdict agreement with no table; shared interval bookkeeping does not merge their discriminating questions.

A probes adaptive selection when reachable influential flags bind a threshold; C conditions zero access on all flagged predictions agreeing. Efficiency among influential rows and invariance-based removal of all access are distinct tests, despite common zero-contribution arithmetic.

Both use unresolved paired-contribution intervals, threshold-sensitive selection versus fixed IDs, frozen full-key checking and bounded unresolved outcomes. A's nearest-failure-then-total hierarchy and D's possible-decision ranking refine the same selection mechanism; D's explicit joint-infeasibility caveat does not add a new causal test.

Both rank flagged rows by acceptance influence using identical contribution intervals and compare supported/unresolved decisions within the same allowances. E substitutes gain-first for fixed-ID rival ordering and a general clause-influence ranking; these instantiate the same selection-efficiency question without establishing another causal mechanism.

B removes confusion cells while preserving bounded adjudication and compares constructed carriers. C removes sealed-row access under an unconfirmed prediction-agreement condition. Neither removed dependency nor predicted observable is the same.

B isolates carrier necessity with identical selected rows and expects verdict coincidence; D changes row selection and predicts fewer adjudications than fixed ordering. Their shared ledger/bounds do not make these interventions equivalent.

B's matched selection tests table-free verdict computation; E's changed selection tests frontier advantage against gain-first ordering. The table-presence observable and selection-dependent supported verdict versus unresolved are different.

C uses a conditional all-agreement audit to remove any adjudication; D selects influential differing-prediction rows by acceptance impact. Both may stop without access on invariant inputs, but C's explicit necessity-removal test differs from D's ordering-efficiency intervention.

C predicts zero-access advance only in its hypothetical all-agreement case; E tests frontier selection versus gain-first when disputed contributions can influence acceptance. Shared invariant-row handling does not make these whole-card causal tests equivalent.

Both replace provisional counts with per-record contribution intervals and prioritize acceptance-sensitive rows, preserving caps and unresolved outcomes. The fixed-ID versus gain-first rival and priority details change the comparison baseline, while the causal question remains whether influence-based selection improves bounded certification.

One structurally valid opening and empty lineage agree with no prior sources. Common bounded-probe requirements are substantially met, but O-52506f6a8d6811274ac6 requires labeled mechanism→demand→response→mechanism arrows, a removable return link and an equal-demand sham; these are absent. 'No ... closing-feedback loop is claimed' does not execute that assigned operator.

Two openings, empty lineage and explicit necessity challenges respect the source shape. Table removal has a source-compatible ledger counterexample and matched carrier probe. The zero-access opening keeps its indispensable agreement assumption unconfirmed and predicts identical advance without explicit ordinary-access observations. Thus logical challenge is executed, while the common discriminating-prediction requirement is partial across the unit.

One opening and empty lineage match the source contract. O-017012b1792011ea58c7 calls for ordinary outcome-directed alternatives and constraints: the bound-based decision rule, fixed-ID rival, withheld/cap accounting and explicit defeat/resource uncertainty satisfy that instruction. No special operator is required.

One opening and empty lineage match the source contract. O-08fa691abb50913ec339 permits generic exploration: the acceptance-frontier action, gain-first rival, differing verdict/unresolved observation, bounded matched-copy probe and explicit defeat assumptions satisfy it. This judgment establishes proposal fit, not measured performance.
